summary: Johann Friedrich Blumenbach studied at Ernestinum Gotha, the University of Jena, and the University of Göttingen. He worked in history, archaeology, and other fields, holding a post at the University of Göttingen from circa 1776 to 1840.
Johann Friedrich Herbart was a philosopher who studied at the University of Jena from 1794 to 1797. He later held a position at the University of Göttingen from circa 1802 to 1809.

Johann Gildemeister worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen under Heinrich Ewald and at Bonn under Georg Wilhelm Freytag, Christian Lassen, and August Wilhelm von Schlegel, later serving as professor at Marburg (1845–1859) and Bonn (1859–1890).

Johann Gottfried Eichhorn worked in religious studies and linguistics. After studying at the University of Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne (1770–1774), he served as professor of Oriental languages at Jena (1775) and professor of philosophy at Göttingen (1788).

Johann Gottfried Ludwig Kosegarten studied under Ernst Moritz Arndt, Hermann Baier, at Greifswald, and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. Working in Indology and linguistics, he held posts at Greifswald (adjunct 1815, professor 1824–1850) and Jena (professor 1817–1824).

Herder worked in philosophy, linguistics, and religious studies, studying at Königsberg under Immanuel Kant. He held posts at the Collegium Fridericianum, Riga Cathedral School, and Wilhelm-Ernst-Gymnasium Weimar, and served as General Superintendent in Saxe-Weimar-Eisenach in 1776.

Johann Gustav Stickel worked in linguistics and other fields. He studied at the University of Jena (1823–1826) and under Johann Gottfried Ludwig Kosegarten and Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, later serving as professor at Jena from 1830 to 1836.
Johann II Bernoulli studied at the University of Basel from circa 1724 to 1729. He later held a post at the University of Basel from circa 1743 to 1790.

Johann III Bernoulli was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Basel, University of Neuchâtel, and under Daniel Bernoulli. He was a member of the Prussian Academy of Sciences, Russian Academy of Sciences, and Naturforschende Gesellschaft in Danzig.
Johann Jakob Engel was a philosopher who studied at the University of Rostock from circa 1757 to 1762 and at Leipzig University from circa 1765 to 1769.

Johann Joachim Winckelmann worked in history and archaeology. He studied at Köllnisches Gymnasium (1736), Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1738–1740), and the University of Jena (1741–1742).

Johann Tobias Beck studied at the University of Tübingen from circa 1822 to 1826. Working in religious studies, he held posts at the University of Basel (circa 1836–1843) and the University of Tübingen (circa 1843–1878).

Johanna Engelberta van Lohuizen-de Leeuw studied at Leiden and Utrecht under Jan Gonda. In Indology and archaeology, she taught at Cambridge and Groningen before directing the Institute of South Asian Archaeology at the University of Amsterdam from 1958 to 1983.

Johanna Narten worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at Saarland under Ernst Zinn and at Erlangen-Nuremberg under Karl Hoffmann, where she earned a PhD and habilitation, later serving as an assistant there (1973–1977).

Johannes Beltz completed his PhD in 1999 at the University of Lausanne and the École Pratique des Hautes Études, studying under Marie-Louise Reiniche and Johannes Bronkhorst. His fields include Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies.

Johannes Bronkhorst studied at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, University of Rajasthan, Pune under S. D. Joshi, and Leiden. Specializing in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, he served as a professor at the University of Lausanne from 1987 to 2011 (and circa 1987–2025).

Johannes Gijsbertus de Casparis worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Leiden University (circa 1934–1939) and held posts at SOAS University of London (circa 1965–1978) and as a professor at Leiden University (1978–1986).

Johannes Hertel studied at Leipzig University (1892–1897). In the field of Indology, he held a professorship at Lessing-Gymnasium Döbeln (circa 1898–1920) and held the chair for Indian Philology at Leipzig University from 1919 to 1937.

Johannes Klatt was an Indologist who studied under Albrecht Weber and earned a doctorate at the University of Halle-Wittenberg. From 1872 onward, he held positions at the Berlin State Library, serving as assistant, custodian, and librarian.

Johannes Nobel studied at Greifswald and Berlin under Heinrich Lüders. Working in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, he worked at the Berlin State Library, taught at the University of Berlin, and held the Indology chair at Marburg from 1928 to 1955.
